questions.prompt: What is the name of the small program that runs at power-up or reboot and loads the kernel? (two words)
Why is the bootstrap program stored in ROM or EEPROM rather than in main memory?
options: Main memory can only hold data, not programs
So that the user can edit it easily
ROM is faster than every other kind of memory
Main memory is empty at power-up, so the first program must live in storage that survives power loss

questions.prompt: Software stored in hardware such as ROM or EEPROM is generally known as ______. (one word)
Which of these is NOT a job of the bootstrap program?
options: Initializing the system: registers, device controllers, memory
Scheduling user programs on the CPU for the rest of the day

questions.prompt: The bootstrap program is loaded at power-up or reboot.
Put the startup steps in order.
options: Run the bootstrap program, initialize the system, load and start the kernel
Load the kernel, initialize the system, run the bootstrap program
Start the kernel, run the bootstrap program, initialize the system
Initialize the system, start the kernel, run the bootstrap program
